questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: distinguish a function from a general relation
questions.stem: A rule pairs each student with the set of books they have borrowed. Why might this rule fail to be a function?

options.text: One student may have borrowed several books, so one input maps to multiple outputs

options.misconception: confuses non-emptiness of outputs with the one-output rule

options.misconception: believes functions only pair numbers

options.text: The rule is a function because each book has a unique borrower
options.misconception: confuses the direction of the pairing

questions.explanation: A function requires each input to have exactly one output, and a student with several borrowed books would have multiple outputs. A relation imposes no such restriction. The trap is assuming every pairing of real objects is automatically a function.

options.text: All x with x at least 4

options.text: All x with x at most 4

questions.topic: Finding a domain from two restrictions
questions.learningObjective: find a domain from two restrictions
questions.stem: A function has denominator x minus 6 and a square root of x minus 1. What is the smallest integer in its domain? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The radicand requires x at least 1 and the denominator requires x not equal to 6, so the smallest integer in the domain is 1. The value 6 is excluded but is not the smallest. The trap is reporting 6, which is excluded but not the minimum.
questions.hint: Find the smallest value satisfying the radicand restriction, then check it is not excluded.
